title: PTWC tsunami timing scores changed from 41% to 64% within 10 minutes when earthquakes had equal weight, 2015-2026
abstract: We checked first point-specific PTWC tsunami arrival estimates against a fixed NCEI archive. We parsed 5,672 issued ETA rows from 2014-2026 and matched each first forecast place to its closest coastal gauge within 20 km. Of 210 nearby forecast-place pairs in 43 earthquakes, 103 lacked a first-arrival clock. The 107 timed pairs in 19 earthquakes span 2015-2026. Forty-four arrivals were within 10 minutes: 41.1% of points. With each earthquake given equal weight, the mean share was 64.3% (95% earthquake-bootstrap range 47.2-80.4%). The equal-earthquake mean recorded-minus-forecast error was +7.3 minutes (-0.9 to +17.2), so the primary test did not establish overall bias. An unadjusted delay trend was +3.11 minutes per forecast hour. After earthquake and place effects were removed, only seven earthquakes supplied identifying variation and the bootstrap was unstable. A travel-speed cause was not established. Without assumptions about missing clocks, the within-10-minute point share over all 210 nearby pairs is only bounded by 21-70%. A separate bounded-delay calculation gives exact sensitivity limits for uncertain first-wave picks. These checks extend a prior height-category study to a different operational target. They do not verify all PTWC forecasts, establish physical onset times, or justify a warning-time correction. Code, source hashes, original figures, aggregate results and all resampling draws are included. Raw records and matched record-level tables stay outside the baseline package.

display.caption: Point and earthquake weights give different timed-sample scores. Missing clocks permit a wide all-nearby-point score range. The right panel gives hypothetical bounds on the adjusted slope under nonnegative arrival-pick delays; it is not a confidence interval.
Earthquake mean timing errors and prespecified sensitivity tests. Positive error means the recorded wave arrived later than forecast. Intervals resample whole earthquakes.

The adjusted travel-time slope has weak identification. Its ranges omit failed resamples and are diagnostic, not unconditional confidence intervals. Travel groups at right were added after initial results and have only 18, 6 and 4 earthquakes.
